[[Category:Philosophical method]]
'''Common sense''' refers to direct sensory perception shared by many human beings, such as vision, hearing, and smell.<ref>{{#cite:Q1837}}</ref>

Trusting common sense means accepting witnessing as a proof of physical existence. e.g., not doubting the existence of one's left hand, which one sees and feels, as an illusion of one's brain.

== Limitations ==

Overtrusting common sense can amount to [[naive empiricism]].
